explanation: Windows lost power unexpectedly while the storage subsystem was reporting hardware and NTFS errors. The system drive may be failing.
Windows Update and servicing failures point to corruption in the component store used to repair system files.
System File Checker or Windows servicing reported damaged protected files.

cause: Windows Update cache or services are unhealthy
explanation: Update failures coincide with disabled update services or repeated update installation errors.
Driver errors and recent blue-screen evidence identify a kernel driver as a likely source of instability.

cause: The computer is under sustained memory pressure
explanation: Available memory is low and Windows is recording resource exhaustion symptoms.
One or more core Microsoft Defender protections are not active, reducing protection against malware.
Adapter or TCP/IP errors occur together with connectivity failures.

cause: DNS resolver state is stale or unhealthy
explanation: Name-resolution errors are present while the network adapter remains connected.

cause: A required Windows service is repeatedly failing
explanation: A critical automatic service is stopped or has generated repeated Service Control Manager failures.

cause: Startup applications are degrading sign-in performance
explanation: A large startup workload is likely increasing sign-in time and background resource use.
Display-driver recovery or GPU errors correlate with application crashes or blue screens.
